dedupe_keys.name: mapping three decades of urban growth in china a 30m annual building height dataset 1990 2019

description: The China annual building-height dataset research team publishes 30 m maps of building height for 1990–2019. Its Figshare description attributes the estimates to multisource satellite imagery and machine learning, with annual coverage intended to represent both horizontal and vertical urban growth. The repository exposes a tiled collection of TIFF files and identifies the dataset as openly licensed CC-BY-4.0, with free access. This is a modelled raster product, not a building-by-building survey. Tile band ordering, units, uncertainty fields and observation consistency were not checked inside the files, so users must inspect the accompanying publication and file metadata before temporal comparisons. The maps could help reconstruct building-volume exposure or historical urban demand inputs for infrastructure simulations. They complement data-cnbh-10m-china-building-height-2020 with a longer annual sequence at a coarser grid. Differences in resolution and estimation methods prevent interpreting a direct raster subtraction as a verified change in individual buildings.
